newsitem.title: USA: Prime suspect dies in famed Florida murder case.
newsitem.headline: Prime suspect dies in famed Florida murder case.

text.p: A serial killer who confessed and then recanted in one of Florida's most famous murder mysteries, the 1981 slaying of 6-year-old Adam Walsh, has died, authorities said Wednesday.
Ottis Toole died on Sept. 15 at a state prison in Lake Butler, Florida, prison officials said. The cause of death was cirrhosis of the liver, according to media reports.

Homicide investigators hoped Toole did not take the secret of the boy's death to his grave -- that he had made a deathbed confession or that his death would bring new witnesses to light, police said Wednesday.

Toole was long the prime suspect in the brutal slaying of Walsh, abducted from a department store in Hollywood, Florida July 27, 1981. The boy's head was found two weeks later in a canal in Vero Beach, 120 miles to the north.

Toole, 49, confessed to scores of murders and was serving five life sentences for several arson murders unrelated to the Walsh case. No relative claimed his body and he was buried at Union Correctional Insitution in Raiford, Florida.

He confessed to killing Adam Walsh in late 1984 but later recanted. Although he was never charged with the crime, he remained a prime suspect because of blood found on the floor of his car and on a machete he once told police he used to cut off the boy's head.
A DNA link was never established and evidence in the case, including the car, disappeared. But police said Wednesday that Toole remained until his death their strongest suspect.
"We're hoping this may be a turn in the investigation," said Hollywood Police spokeswoman Stephanie Norris.

"There may be people that for one of many reasons didn't want to come forward while he was alive," she said. "Perhaps they didn't want to see Ottis go to the electric chair. Perhaps they were afraid. That fear is no longer there."

Norris said investigators would try to interview anyone who had contact with Toole during his final days, including medical personnel and clergy, to determine if he made any "dying declaration" on the killing. She said investigators would like to have talked to Toole before he died but were not told of his illness.

Adam's father, John Walsh, who gained fame following the death of his son as the host of the anti-crime television show "America's Most Wanted," told Miami Fox affiliate WSVN: "This is just another setback, just another heartbreak. You know what this means to my family? No closure. No closure."
